full_judgment: 11. It appears that both the trial Court and the learned judge of the High Court Division while dealing with the question of title totally failed to take notice of the relevant provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1950, briefly the Act, pertaining to the provisions relating to arrear rents etc. and their realisation which accured prior to their vesting in the Government under Clause (C) of Sub-section (4) of section 3 or under Clause (7) of Section 44 of the Act. The learned Assistant Judge thoroughly misdirected himself in taking the view that the rent suit, execution proceeding etc. were to continue under the old law i.e. the Bengal Tenancy Act notwithstanding the promulgation of the Act in 1951. He observed that the sale in question could be held legally and validly under the old law by reason of Section 6 and 7 of the General Clauses Act. Having further found that there was a valid rent sale on 10.9.56 and Abdul Latif obtained delivery of possession from the judgment debtors, it was held that the plaintiffs title was genuine and true.
